why: The tip blade seals at 0.3-1.5 cm for /t/, and partly closed it gives a 0.05-0.15 cm2 channel at the ridge for /s/. The front cavity there is short, so the hiss should land in 4000-8000 Hz. For /tɑ/, the body pad holds the pharyngeal /ɑ/ constriction during the closure, so the rail servo no longer has to make the 79-degree trip it needs now. I also set the body stroke to 1.3 cm, which gives the velar seal for /k/ and the /ʃ/ channel. For /kɑ/, the move from a velar seal near 8.5 cm to the pharyngeal /ɑ/ near 9.5 cm is about 15 degrees on the rail servo (106 degrees over 7 cm). Whether the cam's height change also stays under 30 degrees, the trial will decide. Bill: pushrod_kit $4 (2 days), servo_mg90s x4 on hand, rail_100mm reused. The brief prices the swap at $12, 3 days and 76 machine minutes, all within budget.

The drawstring takes the lip opening to 0 cm2, which seals for /p/ while the tongue is lowered to keep the airway open. Narrowing the lips to a small opening, with the ring pushed out 1.6 cm (the tube goes from 14.5 to 16.1 cm, about 10% lower overall), and a back tongue constriction should pull F2 down toward 840-1020 Hz and F1 down toward 300-570 Hz. That covers /ɔ/, /ʊ/ and /u/. Bill: pushrod_kit $4 (2 days), 2 servos reused, 57 machine minutes.

At 13.2 formants rise about 2.2%: F1 is about 661 at the current posture and F2 about 1173. This is a hedge on proposal 1 that trades a little F1 margin for more F2 margin, in case the 13.0 failure was F2 noise with more spread than I estimate. Even 2 to 4 Hz of extra F1 headroom lets System 1 lift the vowel tip a few hundredths, and that is all a 2° cut needs.
